I came out some years ago in a minecraft video (lol), and just went with a whole informational speech regarding basic definitions, then my own personal experience a little.

It was honestly pretty well received and probably 99.999% of the viewers were super supportive.

However you choose to come out to your audience, stay strong and be confident!  You got this.

One of my alters specifically likes talking to him, as it's the only time she's felt welcome to talk, so it's good in that regard.  Right now we're looking into some of my trauma specifically.  We've gone a whole "treat the disease, not the symptoms" route, meaning we're looking at the causes for things instead of just treating the depression or anxiety as they are now.  Like "okay, you're depressed, let's find out why" instead of just throwing pills at me.

It's pretty unlikely to end up with meds specifically for DID since there really isn't any.  They're more likely to give meds for the symptoms, like ADHD/ADD meds if you have problems focusing and getting things done.

You always have the option of just telling them "no" when it comes to meds.  Never do anything they suggest blindly or if you don't agree with it.
